title: Efficacy and safety of intravenous lidocaine versus placebo associated with intrathecal morphine analgesia in major digestive or abdominal surgery
official: A phase III, randomized, double-blind study assessing the efficacy and safety of intravenous lidocaine versus placebo in patients receiving intrathecal morphine analgesia in major digestive or abdominal surgery by laparotomy
summary: Main objective: To assess the superiority of IV lidocaine combined with morphine rachi anaesthesia compared with placebo combined with morphine rachi anaesthesia, in reducing morphine consumption postoperatively at 48 hours, in patients undergoing major digestive or abdominal surgery under laparotomy.
conditions: Major patients receiving morphine spinal anaesthesia for major gastrointestinal or abdominal surgery by scheduled laparotomy.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 18 years
2. Major digestive or abdominal surgery (pancreatic, hepatic, colorectal, gynaecological, oesophageal, gastric, duodenal, small intestine, etc.)
3. Scheduled intervention
4. Laparotomy
5. Patient in agreement with rachi morphine anaesthesia
6. Membership of a social security scheme
7. Signed informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Emergency surgery
2. Severe liver failure
3. Morphine allergy
4. Allergy to lidocaine
5. Gabapentinoids: pregabalin (Lyrica), gabapentin
6. Patient taking part in another clinical trial, or in a period of exclusion from another clinical trial
7. Inability to understand information relating to the study (for linguistic, psychological or cognitive reasons, or due to a lack of literacy skills)
8. Women who are or may become pregnant (of childbearing age, without effective contraception) or who are breast-feeding
9. Patient deprived of liberty or under guardianship or unable to give consent
10. Rhythm disorder at risk of sudden death (e.g. Brugada syndrome)
11. Flecaine as usual treatment
12. Chronic pain with level II or III analgesics
13. Contraindication to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs: history of peptic ulcer disease, stage 3 A renal failure or more (DFG according to CKD EPI < 60 ml/min).
14. Previous bradycardia and/or known conduction disorder (atrioventricular block) / Pacemaker
15. Unstable coronary
16. Myocardial infarction <6 months
17. Severe cardiocirculatory insufficiency
